newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists would re-nationalise some firms.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists would re-nationalise some firms.

text.p: France's opposition Socialists would cancel the planned privatisation of electronics company Thomson SA and telecommunications utility France Telecom if they returned to power in 1998, party spokesman Francois Hollande said.

Hollande told the daily Liberation in an interview published on Tuesday that a Socialist government would not re-nationalise all companies privatised by the ruling conservatives, since the state was heavily indebted.

"But we do not rule out returning some strategic companies to the state sector on a case-by-case basis," Hollande said. "Two of the privatised companies will have to become state companies again: France Telecom and Thomson."
Hollande said the Socialists would also seek state control of water distribution, currently dominated by two private sector giants -- Generale des Eaux and Lyonnaise des Eaux.
But this could be done through other, unspecified means, rather than nationalisation, he said.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe's centre-right government hopes to raise 25 billion francs ($4.91 billion) from the sale next April of a minority stake in state-owned France Telecom in what is expected to be country's biggest-ever privatisation.
The Socialists are strongly opposing Juppe's plans to sell off defence and consumer electronics Thomson to Lagardere Group for a symbolic price of one franc after a capital injection.
The deal has yet to be approved by the European Commission and France's privatisation commission.
The Socialists, swept from power in a landslide 1993 general election defeat, approved draft economic policy guidelines at a weekend convention for the general election due in March 1998.
Projections published by the conservative daily Le Figaro on Monday suggested the Socialists would make major gains in that vote but fall short of a parliamentary majority.
Hollande said a Socialist government would act pragmatically and would not automatically repurchase 100 percent of the capital of those privatised companies it re-nationalised.
He said it would certainly not nationalise any ailing company to rescue it, but could inject state capital in some promising projects that lacked financing.
